questions.stem: A 58‑year‑old man presents with a 3‑month history of painless jaundice and weight loss. Imaging shows a mass in the head of the pancreas. Which of the following histological features is most characteristic of the most common malignant tumour in this location?
options: Keratinising squamous epithelium with intercellular bridges
Glandular epithelium forming irregular acini with mucin production
Neuroendocrine cells arranged in nests with chromogranin positivity
Spindle‑shaped stromal cells with storiform pattern
questions.explanation: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is the most common pancreatic cancer and shows glandular epithelium forming irregular, poorly‑differentiated ducts with mucin production. Keratinising squamous cells suggest squamous cell carcinoma, neuroendocrine cells indicate a functional tumour, and spindle cells point to a stromal tumour such as a gastrointestinal stromal tumour.
